witnesses.title: The Fly: likeness after injury

selection.locator: The Fly; Songs Y, Bentley plate / object 40, E23. Physical transcription lines 7-10.
selection.limit: Selected quotation and local context; no new candidate decision or whole-work credit.

witnesses.quotation:
Am not I
A fly like thee?
Or art not thou
A man like me?
witnesses.locator: The Fly; Songs Y, Bentley plate / object 40, E23. Physical transcription lines 7-10.
witnesses.credit: William Blake, Songs Y, printed ca. 1825. The Met, Rogers Fund, 1917; 17.10.40. Public Domain / CC0. Complete scan.
witnesses.reading: A thoughtless injury is followed by reciprocal questions. Likeness changes the speaker's relation to a vulnerable other.
witnesses.alternative: The later consolation can also displace the injured fly. Its happiness and consent are not reported.
witnesses.classification_limit: A modern animal sense may lead to Diptera. The analogy supplies neither a species identification nor evidence of insect thought.

witnesses.title: A Dream: capacities in relation

selection.locator: A Dream; Songs Y, Bentley plate / object 26, E16. Physical transcription lines 19-22.
selection.limit: Selected quotation and local context; no new candidate decision or whole-work credit.

witnesses.quotation:
I am set to light the ground,
While the beetle goes his round:
Follow now the beetles hum,
Little wanderer hie thee home.
witnesses.locator: A Dream; Songs Y, Bentley plate / object 26, E16. Physical transcription lines 19-22.
witnesses.credit: William Blake, Songs Y, printed ca. 1825. The Met, Rogers Fund, 1917; 17.10.26. Public Domain / CC0. Complete scan.
witnesses.reading: The emmet is heard before help is offered. Light and the beetle's hum supply different capacities for finding a way home.
witnesses.alternative: The watchman's appointed role can imply ordered offices. The final invitation does not narrate arrival.
witnesses.classification_limit: Emmet can lead conditionally to Formicidae. Glow-worm cannot be allocated to an earthworm lineage by its suffix.

witnesses.title: Thel: a Worm is not a lineage

selection.locator: The Book of Thel F, object 6; Bentley 6 / Erdman plate 4. Physical transcription lines 3-4.
selection.limit: Selected quotation and local context; no new candidate decision or whole-work credit.

witnesses.quotation:
Art thou a Worm? image of weakness. art thou but a Worm?
I see thee like an infant wrapped in the Lillys leaf:
witnesses.locator: The Book of Thel F, object 6; Bentley 6 / Erdman plate 4. Physical transcription lines 3-4.
witnesses.credit: William Blake, Thel (1789), copy F. Library of Congress, Rosenwald 1798A. Printing dates differ. Complete scan; retained LOC rights qualification.
witnesses.reading: Thel sees helpless infancy; the Clay hears a voice and responds. The following plate distinguishes cherishing from punishment of injury.
witnesses.alternative: The infant and the Worm are compared, not anatomically diagnosed. Maternal and nuptial language makes this account of care particular.
witnesses.classification_limit: Worm is a historical body-word, not a clade. Annelid, nematode, flatworm and larval alternatives require context; none is allocated here.
